title: The Strange Case Of Dr. Jekyll And Mr.

facts: The Project Gutenberg eBook of "The Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde" was authored by Robert Louis Stevenson.
The eBook was released on June 27, 2008.
The eBook can be accessed online at www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/43.
The text is credited to David Widger.
Mr. Utterson is a reserved and austere lawyer.
Mr. Hyde trampled a young girl in front of Mr. Enfield.
Mr. Hyde offered compensation to avoid scandal after the incident.
Utterson resolves to investigate the connection between Hyde and a well-known figure.
Mr. Utterson examined Dr. Jekyll's will after dinner.
Dr. Jekyll's will bequeathed all his possessions to Edward Hyde.
Dr. Lanyon had not seen Jekyll in over a decade.
Utterson learned that Hyde had a key to Jekyll's laboratory.
Dr. Jekyll hosted a dinner for a few close friends, including Mr. Utterson.
Utterson expressed his concerns about Jekyll's connection to Mr. Hyde.
Jekyll asked Utterson to promise to look after Hyde's interests after his death.
Utterson reluctantly agreed to help Hyde for Jekyll's sake.
Sir Danvers Carew was murdered by Mr. Hyde in October of 18—.
A maid witnessed Hyde attack Carew with a heavy cane.
Mr. Utterson recognized the broken cane as one he had given to Dr. Henry Jekyll.
Hyde's residence was found to be ransacked during the investigation.
Mr. Utterson visits Dr. Jekyll in the late afternoon.
Dr. Jekyll is shaken by news of a murder involving Edward Hyde.
Mr. Guest notes a resemblance between Hyde's handwriting and a note from Jekyll.
Jekyll expresses a desire to sever ties with Edward Hyde.
Mr. Hyde vanished after the murder of Sir Danvers.
Dr. Jekyll appeared revitalized for over two months after Hyde's disappearance.
Dr. Lanyon declared he was doomed and refused to discuss Jekyll.
Utterson received a letter from Jekyll about a permanent withdrawal from social life.
Mr. Utterson and Mr. Enfield stop in front of the door associated with Mr. Hyde.
Dr. Jekyll appears sad and unwell while sitting by an open window.
Jekyll declines Utterson's invitation to join them outside.
Jekyll suddenly displays a look of terror during their conversation.
Mr. Utterson is visited by Poole, Dr. Jekyll's butler.
Utterson discovers Hyde's lifeless body in Jekyll's cabinet.
Jekyll's will names Utterson as the beneficiary.
Utterson decides to read Jekyll's documents before involving the police.
Dr. Lanyon received a registered letter from Dr. Henry Jekyll on January 9th.
Jekyll instructed Lanyon to retrieve a specific drawer from his cabinet.
Lanyon broke into Jekyll's cabinet with the help of a locksmith.
The mysterious man who arrived at midnight was Jekyll transformed into Hyde.
Dr. Henry Jekyll creates a potion that separates his two identities.
Edward Hyde emerges as a result of Jekyll's scientific exploration.
Hyde commits a murder, leading Jekyll to feel guilt.
Jekyll ultimately succumbs to temptation and loses control over his identity.
